subject: Financial Accounting
title: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader
outline: Purpose and structure of final accounts
Trading Account and cost of goods sold
Profit and Loss Account: expenses and incomes
Year-end adjustments: accruals, prepayments, bad debts and provisions
Depreciation: straight-line, reducing balance and disposal
Interpretation: gross profit margin, mark-up and net profit ratio

modules.title: Trading, Profit and Loss Account
modules.html:
1. The Trading Account

It ascertains gross profit, the excess of net sales over the cost of the goods sold:

$$ \text{Cost of Goods Sold} = \text{Opening Stock} + \text{Net Purchases} + \text{Carriage Inwards} - \text{Closing Stock} $$ $$ \text{Gross Profit} = \text{Net Sales} - \text{Cost of Goods Sold} $$

Net purchases = purchases - returns outwards - goods taken by the owner. Net sales = sales - returns inwards. Carriage inwards is part of cost of goods sold; carriage outwards is a selling expense in the Profit and Loss Account.

2. Specimen (vertical form)

Trading and Profit and Loss Account for the year ended 31 DecNN
Sales6,000,000
Less Returns inwards(150,000)
Net sales5,850,000
Opening stock600,000
Add Purchases (net)3,500,000
Add Carriage inwards100,000
Goods available for sale4,200,000
Less Closing stock(700,000)
Cost of goods sold(3,500,000)
Gross profit2,350,000
Add Discount received, rent received150,000
Less Expenses (salaries, rent, depreciation, bad debts, etc.)(1,300,000)
Net profit1,200,000

3. Capital vs Revenue

Capital expenditure buys or improves a fixed asset (including legal fees, installation and carriage on the asset) and goes to the Balance Sheet. Revenue expenditure is the day-to-day running cost and goes to the Profit and Loss Account. Misclassification distorts both profit and net assets.

4. Useful Ratios

$$ \text{Gross Profit Margin} = \dfrac{\text{Gross Profit}}{\text{Net Sales}} \times 100 $$ $$ \text{Mark-up} = \dfrac{\text{Gross Profit}}{\text{Cost of Goods Sold}} \times 100 $$

examples.q: Opening stock N450,000; purchases N2,800,000; returns outwards N60,000; carriage inwards N90,000; closing stock N520,000; sales N4,100,000; returns inwards N100,000. Compute cost of goods sold, gross profit and the gross profit margin.
A trader marks up goods by 25% on cost. If sales for the year were N3,000,000, what was the cost of goods sold?
examples.a: With a mark-up of 25% on cost, cost = 100 and selling price = 125. Therefore COGS = \( \dfrac{100}{125} \times 3,000,000 = N2,400,000 \) and gross profit = N600,000 (a margin of 20% on sales).

modules.title: Year-End Adjustments
modules.html:
1. Accruals and Prepayments

  • Accrued expense (owing): add to the expense in the P&L and show as a current liability.
  • Prepaid expense: deduct from the expense and show as a current asset.
  • Accrued income (receivable): add to income and show as a current asset.
  • Income received in advance: deduct from income and show as a current liability.

2. Bad Debts and Provisions

A bad debt is written off: Dr Bad Debts, Cr Debtor. A provision for doubtful debts is an estimate on the remaining debtors. Only the increase or decrease in the provision is charged or credited to the Profit and Loss Account, while the full provision is deducted from debtors in the Balance Sheet.

Bad debts recovered: Dr Cash/Bank, Cr Bad Debts Recovered (an income).

3. Depreciation

Depreciation is the systematic allocation of the depreciable amount of a fixed asset over its useful life. Causes: wear and tear, passage of time, obsolescence, depletion and inadequacy.

$$ \text{Straight Line Depreciation} = \dfrac{\text{Cost} - \text{Scrap Value}}{\text{Estimated Life}} $$ $$ \text{Reducing Balance Depreciation} = \text{Net Book Value} \times \text{Rate \%} $$

Entries: Dr Depreciation (P&L), Cr Provision for Depreciation. In the Balance Sheet the asset shows cost less accumulated depreciation = net book value.

On disposal: transfer cost to Disposal Account, transfer accumulated depreciation to Disposal Account, credit proceeds; the balancing figure is profit or loss on disposal.

4. Other Adjustments

  • Goods taken by the owner: Dr Drawings, Cr Purchases.
  • Closing stock: Dr Stock (asset), Cr Trading Account.
  • Provision for discount on debtors, calculated after deducting the provision for doubtful debts.

examples.q: A machine costing N2,000,000 has a scrap value of N200,000 and a useful life of 6 years. Compute annual depreciation on the straight-line basis and the net book value after 4 years.
examples.a: \( \text{Depreciation} = \dfrac{2,000,000 - 200,000}{6} = N300,000 \) per annum. Accumulated depreciation after 4 years = 4 x 300,000 = N1,200,000. Net book value = 2,000,000 - 1,200,000 = N800,000.

examples.q: Equipment costing N800,000 is depreciated at 20% per annum on the reducing balance. Show the charge for the first three years.
examples.a: Year 1: 20% x 800,000 = N160,000; NBV = N640,000. Year 2: 20% x 640,000 = N128,000; NBV = N512,000. Year 3: 20% x 512,000 = N102,400; NBV = N409,600. The charge falls each year because it is computed on a diminishing net book value.

examples.q: Debtors at 31 December are N1,250,000. A debt of N50,000 is to be written off and a provision of 5% created on the remainder. Show the treatment.
examples.a: Write off: Dr Bad Debts N50,000, Cr Debtors N50,000, leaving debtors at N1,200,000. Provision = 5% x 1,200,000 = N60,000: Dr Profit and Loss N60,000, Cr Provision for Doubtful Debts N60,000. Balance Sheet: Debtors N1,200,000 less provision N60,000 = N1,140,000. The P&L is charged with N50,000 + N60,000 = N110,000 in total.

modules.title: The Balance Sheet and Interpretation
modules.html:
1. Vertical Balance Sheet

ItemCost NDepn NNBV N
Premises5,000,000-5,000,000
Motor van2,400,000960,0001,440,000
Fittings800,000240,000560,000
Total fixed assets8,200,0001,200,0007,000,000

Then current assets (stock, debtors less provision, prepayments, bank, cash) less current liabilities (creditors, accruals, overdraft) gives working capital; add to fixed assets to get net assets, financed by capital + net profit - drawings + long-term loans.

2. Order of Presentation

Assets may be arranged in order of permanence (most fixed first, Nigerian examination norm) or in order of liquidity (most liquid first).

3. Key Interpretation Measures

$$ \text{Net Profit Percentage} = \dfrac{\text{Net Profit}}{\text{Net Sales}} \times 100 $$ $$ \text{Current Ratio} = \dfrac{\text{Current Assets}}{\text{Current Liabilities}}, \qquad \text{Acid Test} = \dfrac{\text{Current Assets} - \text{Stock}}{\text{Current Liabilities}} $$ $$ \text{Return on Capital Employed} = \dfrac{\text{Net Profit}}{\text{Capital Employed}} \times 100 $$

A current ratio around 2:1 and an acid test near 1:1 are conventionally regarded as healthy, though the appropriate level depends on the trade.

examples.q: Current assets: stock N900,000, debtors N600,000, bank N300,000. Current liabilities: creditors N700,000, accruals N100,000. Compute working capital, the current ratio and the acid-test ratio.
examples.a: Current assets = N1,800,000; current liabilities = N800,000. Working capital = 1,800,000 - 800,000 = N1,000,000. Current ratio = \( \dfrac{1,800,000}{800,000} = 2.25:1 \). Acid test = \( \dfrac{1,800,000 - 900,000}{800,000} = 1.125:1 \). Both indicate comfortable short-term liquidity.

examples.q: Net profit is N1,200,000, opening capital N4,000,000, drawings N500,000 and no new capital. Compute closing capital and return on opening capital.

modules.title: Purpose and structure of final accounts
modules.html:
Purpose and structure of final accounts is a key part of Final Accounts of a Sole Trader (SSS 2, Financial Accounting). Master the meaning, the main points and how it is tested in JAMB and WAEC questions on this topic.

Key points

  • Learn the meaning of purpose and structure of final accounts and the terms used with it.
  • Know the main types, features or steps involved in purpose and structure of final accounts.
  • Be able to give an example of purpose and structure of final accounts and explain why it matters in final accounts of a sole trader.
  • Practise past questions on purpose and structure of final accounts until you can answer them without notes.

Worked example

Q: Gross profit is the excess of:
A: Net sales over cost of goods sold — Gross profit = net sales less cost of goods sold, computed in the trading account.

Q: Carriage inwards is charged to the:
A: Trading account — Carriage inwards is part of the cost of bringing in goods and is added in the trading account.

examples.q: Gross profit is the excess of:
examples.a: Net sales over cost of goods sold — Gross profit = net sales less cost of goods sold, computed in the trading account.

examples.q: Carriage inwards is charged to the:
examples.a: Trading account — Carriage inwards is part of the cost of bringing in goods and is added in the trading account.

modules.title: Year-end adjustments: accruals, prepayments, bad debts and provisions
modules.html:
Year-end adjustments: accruals, prepayments, bad debts and provisions is a key part of Final Accounts of a Sole Trader (SSS 2, Financial Accounting). Master the meaning, the main points and how it is tested in JAMB and WAEC questions on this topic.

Key points

  • Specimen (vertical form) Trading and Profit and Loss Account for the year ended 31 Dec N N Sales 6,000,000 Less Returns inwards (150,000) Net sales 5,850,000 Opening stock 600,000 Add Purchases (net) 3,500,000 Add Carriage inwards 100,000 Goods available for sale 4,200,000 Less Closing stock (700,000) Cost of goods sold (3,500,000) Gross profit 2,350,000 Add Discount received, rent received 150,000 Less Expenses (salaries, rent, depreciation, bad debts, etc.) (1,300,000) Net profit 1,200,000 3.
  • Capital vs Revenue Capital expenditure buys or improves a fixed asset (including legal fees, installation and carriage on the asset) and goes to the Balance Sheet.
  • Revenue expenditure is the day-to-day running cost and goes to the Profit and Loss Account.
  • Accruals and Prepayments Accrued expense (owing): add to the expense in the P&L and show as a current liability.
  • Bad Debts and Provisions A bad debt is written off: Dr Bad Debts, Cr Debtor.

Worked example

Q: Under the reducing balance method, the annual charge:
A: Decreases yearly — The rate is applied to a falling net book value, so the charge decreases each year.

Q: An expense owing at the year end is:
A: Added to the expense and shown as a liability — Accruals are added to the expense in the P&L and shown as current liabilities.

examples.q: Under the reducing balance method, the annual charge:
examples.a: Decreases yearly — The rate is applied to a falling net book value, so the charge decreases each year.

examples.q: An expense owing at the year end is:
examples.a: Added to the expense and shown as a liability — Accruals are added to the expense in the P&L and shown as current liabilities.

quiz.q: Gross profit is the excess of:
options: Net sales over cost of goods sold
quiz.solution: Gross profit = net sales less cost of goods sold, computed in the trading account.

quiz.q: Carriage inwards is charged to the:
quiz.solution: Carriage inwards is part of the cost of bringing in goods and is added in the trading account.

quiz.q: Closing stock appears:
options: In the trading account and the balance sheet
In the profit and loss account only
quiz.solution: Closing stock is deducted in the trading account and shown as a current asset in the balance sheet.

quiz.q: Cost N1,000,000, scrap N100,000, life 5 years. Straight-line depreciation per annum is:
Under the reducing balance method, the annual charge:
quiz.solution: The rate is applied to a falling net book value, so the charge decreases each year.

quiz.q: An expense owing at the year end is:
options: Deducted from the expense and shown as an asset
Added to the expense and shown as a liability
quiz.solution: Accruals are added to the expense in the P&L and shown as current liabilities.

quiz.q: An increase in the provision for doubtful debts is:
quiz.solution: Only the increase is charged (debited) to the profit and loss account.

quiz.q: Goods withdrawn by the owner for personal use are recorded as:
quiz.solution: The cost of the goods is removed from purchases and charged to drawings.

quiz.q: Which is capital expenditure?
quiz.solution: Installation cost is part of bringing a fixed asset into working condition and is capitalised.

quiz.q: Sales N2,500,000 and gross profit margin 40%. Cost of goods sold is:
The acid-test ratio excludes:
quiz.solution: Stock is the least liquid current asset and is excluded from the quick (acid-test) ratio.

quiz.q: Discount received is shown in the:
options: Credit side of the profit and loss account
Debit side of the trading account
quiz.solution: Discount received is an income added to gross profit in the profit and loss account.

quiz.q: Depreciation is charged in order to:
options: Spread the cost of an asset over its useful life
quiz.solution: Depreciation matches the cost of using the asset with the revenue it helps to earn; it is not a fund of cash.

quiz.q: Prepaid rent at the year end is shown as:
quiz.solution: The unexpired portion is an amount owed to the business in service terms and appears as a current asset.

quiz.q: A van with net book value N500,000 was sold for N620,000. The result is:
quiz.solution: Proceeds exceed net book value by N120,000, which is a profit on disposal credited to the profit and loss account.

quiz.q: Net profit N840,000 on net sales of N4,200,000 gives a net profit percentage of:
Sold goods on credit to John. Accounts affected?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: John and Sales.

quiz.q: In Departmental Accounts, expenses that cannot be directly traced to a department are allocated _____.
options: To the department with highest sales
On a reasonable basis such as floor space or turnover
quiz.solution: Common expenses (like rent or electricity) are apportioned using logical bases (e.g., rent by floor area).

quiz.q: A machine was purchased for #20,000. It is to be depreciated at 10% per annum using the Reducing Balance method. Calculate the depreciation charge for the second year.
An asset with an original cost of #5,000 and a scrap value of #500 has an estimated life of 5 years. Calculate its annual depreciation using the Straight Line method.
quiz.solution: Annual Depreciation = (Cost - Scrap Value) / Estimated Life = (5,000 - 500) / 5 = 4,500 / 5 = #900.

quiz.q: Calculate Depreciation: Cost N10,000, Rate 10% Straight Line.
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: N1,000.

quiz.q: A "Surplus" in non-profit accounts means?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Income exceeds expenditure.

quiz.q: A "Deficit" in non-profit accounts means?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Expenditure exceeds income.

quiz.q: Gross Profit = ₦200, Expenses = ₦50. Net Profit is?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: ₦150.

quiz.q: Purchased goods for cash ₦100. Accounts affected?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Purchases and Cash.

quiz.q: In a partnership, where there is no deed, the Profit and Loss sharing ratio is _____.
quiz.solution: According to the Partnership Act of 1890, in the absence of a formal agreement, profits and losses must be shared equally among partners.

quiz.q: A firm purchased a machine for #10,000. It is estimated to last 4 years with a scrap value of #2,000. Using the straight-line method, calculate the annual depreciation.
quiz.solution: Annual Depreciation = (Cost - Scrap Value) / Life = (10,000 - 2,000) / 4 = 8,000 / 4 = #2,000.

quiz.q: The ledger containing the individual accounts of suppliers is the _____.
quiz.solution: The Purchases Ledger (or Creditors Ledger) houses the personal accounts of all credit suppliers.

quiz.q: The ledger that contains all accounts except personal accounts is the _____.
quiz.solution: The General Ledger (or Impersonal Ledger) contains real and nominal accounts (Asset, Liability, Income, Expense).

quiz.q: The Sales Ledger contains the accounts of _____.
quiz.solution: The Sales Ledger is used to maintain individual accounts for customers (trade debtors) who buy goods on credit.

quiz.q: The ledger that contains all accounts except personal accounts is the _____ ledger.
quiz.solution: The General Ledger houses the real and nominal accounts (impersonal accounts), whereas personal accounts are in the Sales and Purchases ledgers.

quiz.q: Which of the following is recorded in the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account?
quiz.solution: The Appropriation Account is used to show how net profit is distributed among partners (interest on capital, salaries, drawings, shared profit).

quiz.q: The official in charge of the accounts of a government ministry is the _____.
quiz.solution: The Permanent Secretary of a ministry is usually the Accounting Officer, responsible for the funds voted for that ministry.

quiz.q: In Departmental Accounts, rent is usually allocated to departments based on _____.
quiz.solution: Rent is a space-related cost, so it is most logically apportioned based on the physical space (floor area) used by each department.

quiz.q: Calculate Cost of Goods Sold: Opening Stock N500, Purchases N2000, Closing Stock N300.
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: N2200.

quiz.q: Accrued expenses are treated in the Balance Sheet as:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Current Liabilities.

quiz.q: Control Accounts are used to check:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Ledgers.

quiz.q: Cost of Goods Sold is calculated as:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Opening Stock + Purchases - Closing Stock.

quiz.q: Real accounts relate to:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Assets/Properties.

quiz.q: Control accounts are used to:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Check arithmetical accuracy of ledgers.

quiz.q: Departmental accounts are prepared to:
options: Ascertain the performance of each department
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Ascertain the performance of each department.

quiz.q: Straight line depreciation charges:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Fixed amount.

quiz.q: Control Accounts check:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Ledgers.

quiz.q: The process of transferring entries from the journals to the accounts in the ledger is called...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Posting.

quiz.q: Calculate the depreciation of a machine costing ₦10,000 with a scrap value of ₦2,000 and a life span of 4 years using the straight-line method.
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: ₦2,000.

quiz.q: The formula for calculating 'Cost of Goods Sold' is...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Opening Stock + Purchases - Closing Stock.

quiz.q: Accumulated fund is a term used in the accounts of...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Non-profit making organizations.

quiz.q: Control accounts are also known as...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Total accounts.

quiz.q: What is the net profit if Gross Profit is ₦5,000, Rent is ₦500, Salaries are ₦1,200 and Discount Received is ₦200?
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: ₦3,500.

quiz.q: Control Accounts:
quiz.solution: Past question (NECO 2025). Correct answer: Check ledgers.
